# vk v0.4.1

Date: 2026-10-25. Status: Experimental development release.
Cargo package: `vkrust` version `0.4.1+1.4.365`. Rust library/import: `vk`. License: MIT.

## Scope

This release flattens the public binding namespace, extends the opt-in native
allocator with managed images and resource policies, and adds generated Khronos
references and native-name documentation search. Callable coverage remains all
842 selected command spellings in the pinned Vulkan registry, including core
Vulkan 1.0–1.4. This is registry coverage, not Vulkan conformance or full physical
execution qualification.

## Changes

- Put Vulkan and StdVideo bindings directly under `vk::`, with flat source and
  matching tests. `load` and `memory` are the public subsystem modules.
- Keep `Instance` / `Device` as dispatch wrappers and `InstanceHandle` /
  `DeviceHandle` as native ABI identities. Free functions and methods share one
  canonical implementation and cached PFNs.
- Add managed non-disjoint image creation, requirement queries, dedication,
  binding, mapping and explicit cleanup with transactional failure handling.
- Partition buffer, linear-image and optimal-image pool classes. Add bounded
  adaptive block shrinking, reuse before growth, and separate-allocation fallback
  on recoverable storage pressure. Required/preferred native dedication overrides
  pooling and identifies the exact resource.
- Admit reviewed video-profile and image-format-list creation chains without
  retaining caller pointers. Codec contents, feature legality, synchronization
  and native valid usage remain the unsafe caller's responsibility.
- Compile the VMA preference oracle against staged, hash-verified core/video
  headers, with a poisoned umbrella include to catch accidental local SDK use.
- Port VMA automatic memory preferences with 1,600 pinned donor vectors. Add
  explicit heap ceilings and budget snapshots that distinguish native
  EXT_memory_budget queries from local accounting estimates.
- Generate Khronos references and native C search aliases for types, constants,
  enum values, PFNs, commands and record members. Keep the C/Rust ABI field map
  unchanged. StdVideo and registry-only symbols link to pinned source instead of
  fabricated reference pages.
- Share the branded README with the rustdoc introduction, compile its five Rust
  examples, and check rendered links and actual native-name search results.
- Expand package discovery metadata for graphics, compute, game development and
  AI/ML building blocks.

## Compatibility and migration

Use `vk = { package = "vkrust", version = "0.4" }`. Rust 1.98.1 and edition 2024
remain the declared baseline. The `+1.4.365` build metadata identifies the pinned
Vulkan 1.4 headers at revision 365; it does not require a Vulkan 1.4 driver.
The dependency requirement stays `0.4`; application API requests and enabled
capabilities determine runtime compatibility. Default features still enable
library loading;
`allocator` is an explicit opt-in.

The `vk::core` module is removed. Import bindings directly from `vk::`, for example
`vk::ApplicationInfo`, `vk::Buffer` and `vk::StdVideoDecodeVP9PictureInfo`.
Raw instance/device identities remain `InstanceHandle` / `DeviceHandle`.
Native PFN signatures, representations, calling conventions and the ABI name map
are unchanged by the documentation update.

Allocator option records gain automatic usage, host-access, transfer-alternative
and avoided-property fields. Use `..Default::default()` when specifying only
selected options. Default storage remains separate; pooled/adaptive storage is
explicit policy. Allocation tokens may share native memory and have nonzero
offsets. Destroy resources and release allocations explicitly after completion.
No destructor submits, waits or performs native cleanup.

## Verification and limitations

Local checks cover 1,619 Rust cases, including generated API contracts and six
doctests, plus 33 Python tooling tests. Strict Clippy, deterministic generation,
registry order, minimal/default feature tests, warnings-denied rustdoc and the
rendered search checker pass. The release also requires an actual archive and
independent minimal/loader/allocator consumers. Hosted CI runs those gates with
pinned C ABI/PFN/feature oracles, donor allocator comparisons, Windows/macOS host
checks and explicit Lavapipe workloads. Actual workflow results establish the
hosted runner evidence; configured jobs alone do not.

The preceding allocator checkpoint passed native buffer/image readback and
separate core/synchronization validation on x86-64 Linux, Intel HD Graphics 4400
(Haswell), Vulkan 1.2 and Mesa. Managed images, budget queries and adaptive policy
have independent PFN/failure tests. The pinned native VMA buffer comparison
covers 96 traces / 64,944 operations; it does not prove complete image or VMA
policy equivalence.

The allocator remains work in progress. Mixed-class block packing, custom pools,
defragmentation, broad external/disjoint/protected memory paths, shared
concurrency and comparative performance qualification remain open. Positive
video/WSI/ray-tracing, physical Vulkan 1.3/1.4, other devices and architectures
remain separate qualification gates. No VMA parity, universal safety, production
readiness or speed advantage is claimed. See
[qualification and limitations](../qualification.md).

## Distribution

Private and public lanes share package version `0.4.1+1.4.365` and release tag
`v0.4.1`, with independent
Git histories. Public source contains no private engineering documents or
agent/editor configuration. The sanitized snapshot records its exact private
source commit. Public history advances only `main`.

The release pipeline publishes the verified Cargo archive and checks registry
metadata and downloaded bytes. GitHub release assets include that exact archive,
the Rust API reference, SHA-256 checksums and build evidence. Published versions
and tags are immutable.
